title: Rayleigh scattering across the visible
caption: Scattering by air molecules goes as 1/λ⁴. Taking 700 nm light as 1, 450 nm light is scattered (700/450)⁴ = 5.9 times as strongly and violet (400 nm) over nine times, so scattered blue fills the sky while the unscattered red and orange remain at sunset.
alt: Graph of relative scattering against wavelength from 400 to 700 nanometres: a curve falling from about 9.4 at 400 nm through 5.9 at 450 nm to 1 at 700 nm.
description: The horizontal axis is wavelength in nanometres across the visible band; the vertical axis is the scattered intensity relative to that of 700 nm light.
The curve is (700/λ)⁴, from the Rayleigh law I ∝ 1/λ⁴.
At 450 nm it is (700/450)⁴ = 5.9; at 700 nm it is 1; at 400 nm it is 9.4.
Short wavelengths are scattered out of the beam far more than long ones.
